entries.learning_activity:
(a) Analyse 
forms of

East and 
West African 
societies
teaching_learning_activities:
Scenario: Set up a 
scenario that shows 
various Fine Arts works 
and analyse forms of Fine 
Arts (drawings, paintings 
and prints)

Library search: Assign 
students in groups to 
search information from 
various sources about the 
management of drawings, 
paintings and prints in 
East and West African 
societies

Jigsaw: Guide Students 
to analyse tools, materials 
and social functions of 
drawings, paintings and 
prints in East and West 
African

Forms of Fine 
Art (drawing, 
paintings and 
prints) in East 
and West African 
societies are well 
analysed

Art works  
(drawings,

prints)

entries.specific_competence:
2.1  Create still 
and moving 
images
entries.learning_activity:
(a)  Create single 
object still 
images using 
drawing and 
painting 
methods
teaching_learning_activities:
Think-ink- pair –share: 
Guide students to discuss 
the concepts of still 
and moving images 
(animation)

Project work: Guide 
sudents in small 
groups to employ basic 
principles of Fine Arts to 
create still and moving 
images (animation) by 
drawing and painting 
methods

Exhibition: Guide 
sudents display the 
pictures for class  
discussion
entries.assessment:
Single object 
still images 
using drawing 
and painting 
methods are 
well created
resources:
Manila paper, 
canvas, pencils, 
paints (Water 
colors, acrylic, 
and oil colours, 
painting 
brushes, 
palette, linseed 
oil, water, 
painting and  
containers,metal 
peg bar, ruler, 
compass, 
stapler, glue, 
push pins, 
sketch book 
and transparent 
sheets
entries.references: TIE, Fine Art for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.specific_competence:
2.2  Create 
artistic 
works using 
various 
techniques
entries.learning_activity:
(a) Create prints 
of various 
motifs
teaching_learning_activities:
ICT-based learning: 
Guide students in small 
groups to identify the 
various techniques of 
making different motifs

Discussion: The teacher 
to display motifs of 
different subjects and 
conduct discussion with 
students on the nature, 
shapes of the motifs and 
the techniques used to 
create the motifs

Hands-on activities: 
Guide the students to 
make various shapes 
of motifs to be used on 
surface to create prints

Exhibition:  Guide 
students to display 
their artworks for class 
discussion
entries.assessment:
Prints of various 
motifs are well 
created
resources:
Screen, mesh, 
printing colours, 
squeegee, 
painting 
brushes, photo-
emulsion, 
sensitizer, 
paste, water, 
white papers, 
dish, a piece 
of transparent 
glass, frame for 
screen mesh, 
cloth materials, 
wood glue, 
office glue, shoe 
tacks, hammer, 
masking 
tapes, pencils, 
black ink/pen, 
computer, and 
printer
entries.references: TIE, Fine Art for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.specific_competence:
2.2  Create 
artistic 
works using 
various 
techniques
entries.learning_activity:
(b)   Create relief detailed realistic 
sculptures
teaching_learning_activities:
Exploration: Guide 
the students to conduct 
a survey to find out 
the tool and materials 
required in making 
realistic sculptures

Demonstration: The 
teacher to use sculpting 
tools and techniques 
to make detailed 
and realistic relief  
sculptures for students 
to observe and discuss 
on the process of making 
sculptures

Hands-on activities: 
Guide students to 
use tools and employ 
techniques in making a 
detailed realistic relief 
sculpture

Exhibition:  Guide 
students to display 
artworks for class 
discussion
entries.assessment:
Detailed 
relief realistic 
sculptures are 
well created
resources:
Chisels, 
carving knives 
mallets, over-
coat, various 
species of wood, 
soapstone, clay, 
plaster, papier 
mache, metals,  
various size of 
sand-papers, 
vanish,  and 
adze
entries.references: TIE, Fine Art for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

sculptures
teaching_learning_activities:
Exploration: Guide 
the students to conduct 
a survey to find out 
the tool and materials 
required in making 
realistic sculptures

Demonstration: The 
teacher to use sculpting 
tools and techniques 
to make detailed 
and realistic relief  
sculptures for students 
to observe and discuss 
on the process of making 
sculptures

Hands-on activities: 
Guide students to 
use tools and employ 
techniques in making a 
detailed realistic relief 
sculpture

Exhibition:  Guide 
students to display 
artworks for class 
discussion
entries.assessment:
Detailed 
relief realistic 
sculptures are 
well created
resources:
Chisels, 
carving knives 
mallets, over-
coat, various 
species of wood, 
soapstone, clay, 
plaster, papier 
mache, metals,  
various size of 
sand-papers, 
vanish,  and 
adze
entries.references: TIE, Fine Art for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education
